### 1. What Turbonomic brings to the table | Feature | What Turbonomic does | Why it matters for Unilever | |---------|----------------------|-----------------------------| | **AI‑driven continuous optimization** | Uses machine‑learning models to predict the impact of every change (CPU, memory, storage, network) on performance, cost, and compliance. | Unilever can run thousands of workloads (e.g., e‑commerce, supply‑chain analytics, marketing AI) across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem, and let Turbonomic automatically shift them to the most efficient place in real time. | | **Unified multi‑cloud observability** | Pulls telemetry from all clouds into a single pane of glass – metrics, logs, events, cost data, and policy violations. | No more “cloud‑by‑cloud” dashboards. Unilever’s ops, finance, and security teams see one consistent view of the entire environment. | | **Policy‑based automation** | Define high‑level business rules (“keep latency < 200 ms”, “stay under $X per month”, “enforce GDPR data residency”). Turbonomic enforces them automatically. | Reduces manual toil, eliminates drift, and guarantees that every workload stays compliant with corporate and regulatory policies. | | **Cost forecasting & budgeting** | Projects future spend based on current usage patterns and planned changes. | Unilever can set budgets per product line or region and get alerts before overspending. | | **Capacity planning & right‑sizing** | Continuously recommends right‑size instances, autoscaling thresholds, and spot‑instance usage. | Cuts waste, improves performance, and keeps the cloud bill predictable. | | **Integration with CI/CD & DevOps** | Can be triggered by GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or Terraform to automatically adjust resources during deployments. | Enables “shift‑left” cost optimization—optimizations happen as part of the development pipeline. | --- ### 2. How Turbonomic can help Unilever specifically | Unilever challenge | Turbonomic solution | Expected outcome | |--------------------|---------------------|------------------| | **Multi‑cloud complexity** | Unified telemetry + AI recommendations across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem | One dashboard, one set of policies, reduced cognitive load | | **Cost overruns** | Real‑time cost alerts, right‑sizing, spot‑instance optimization | 10–30 % reduction in cloud spend (industry benchmark) | | **Performance variability** | Predictive workload placement, autoscaling, capacity alerts | Consistent latency for customer‑facing services | | **Compliance & security** | Policy enforcement (data residency, encryption, audit trails) | Fewer audit findings, faster remediation | | **Operational agility** | Automation of scaling, migration, and decommissioning | Faster time‑to‑market for new features and experiments | *Example scenario:* Unilever launches a new AI‑driven demand‑forecasting model that spikes during holiday seasons. Turbonomic detects the spike, predicts the impact on downstream services, and automatically migrates the model to a cheaper spot‑instance pool in GCP while keeping latency within SLA. When the season ends, it moves the workload back to a reserved instance in Azure, saving cost without human intervention. --- ### 3. Turbonomic vs. Native Cloud‑Provider Tools | Capability | Turbonomic | GCP (Stackdriver/Cloud Monitoring) | AWS (CloudWatch/Cost Explorer) | Azure (Monitor/Advisor) | |------------|------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + on‑prem | Single‑cloud | Single‑cloud | Single‑cloud | | **Observability** | Unified metrics, logs, events, cost, policy violations | Metrics & logs per service | Metrics & logs per service | Metrics & logs per service | | **AI/ML** | Continuous optimization engine, predictive modeling | Limited ML (e.g., anomaly detection) | Limited ML | Limited ML | | **Automation** | Policy‑driven actions (scale, migrate, terminate) | Manual alarms + Lambda/Automation | Manual alarms + Lambda/Automation | Manual alerts + Automation | | **Cost Management** | Forecasting, budgeting, right‑sizing, spot‑optimization | Cost Explorer, Budgets | Cost Explorer, Budgets | Advisor, Cost Management | | **Compliance** | Policy enforcement (GDPR, SOC, ISO) | Logging & audit | Logging & audit | Logging & audit | | **Ease of Use** | Single UI, single API | Multiple consoles, provider‑specific APIs | Multiple consoles, provider‑specific APIs | Multiple consoles, provider‑specific APIs | | **Vendor Lock‑in** | None (works across clouds) | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | Vendor‑specific | #### Key differences 1. **Cross‑cloud intelligence** - *Native tools* only see what happens inside their own cloud. - *Turbonomic* aggregates telemetry from all clouds, so it can recommend moving a workload from AWS to Azure if that saves money or improves latency. 2. **Real‑time AI optimization** - *Native tools* provide dashboards and alerts; you still need to act. - *Turbonomic* runs a continuous optimization loop that automatically takes action (e.g., scale up/down, migrate, terminate) based on your policies. 3. **Unified policy enforcement** - *Native tools* enforce policies only within their own cloud. - *Turbonomic* lets you write a single policy that applies to all clouds, ensuring consistent compliance. 4. **Cost forecasting & budgeting** - *Native tools* give you spend reports and simple budgets. - *Turbonomic* predicts future spend under different scenarios (e.g., adding a new workload, changing instance types) and alerts you before you hit a budget. 5. **Operational agility** - *Native tools* require you to manually trigger scaling or migrations. - *Turbonomic* can hook into CI/CD pipelines and automatically adjust resources as part of the deployment process. --- ### 4. Implementation Roadmap for Unilever | Phase | Activities | Deliverables | |-------|------------|--------------| | **Discovery** | • Inventory all workloads (cloud, on‑prem).
• Map performance SLAs, cost budgets, compliance requirements. | • Workload inventory
• Baseline performance & cost metrics | | **Pilot** | • Deploy Turbonomic in a single region (e.g., EU‑West).
• Connect to AWS, Azure, GCP APIs.
• Define a few high‑impact policies (e.g., “auto‑scale e‑commerce front‑end”). | • Pilot dashboard
• First set of optimization recommendations | | **Scale** | • Roll out to all regions.
• Integrate with CI/CD (GitHub Actions, Terraform).
• Enable cost forecasting. | • Multi‑region unified view
• Automated scaling & migration | | **Governance** | • Formalize policy library (performance, cost, compliance).
• Set up alerts & dashboards for finance & security. | • Policy catalog
• Governance dashboards | | **Optimization Loop** | • Continuous monitoring, fine‑tune policies.
• Quarterly cost‑saving reports. | • Ongoing optimization insights
• ROI metrics | --- ### 5. Bottom Line - **Turbonomic** gives Unilever a single, AI‑powered platform that turns raw telemetry from AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem into actionable insights and automated actions. - It removes the “cloud‑by‑cloud” silos that native tools create, enabling true multi‑cloud observability, cost control, and compliance. - By automating scaling, migration, and right‑sizing, Unilever can focus on innovation rather than firefighting, while keeping spend predictable and within policy bounds.
